items.title: Introduction
items.text:
Welcome to AI-VERDE, an open source platform that facilitates access to commercial and on-premise LLMs with budget and access controls. AI-VERDE stands for "AI Virtual Explorer for Research, Discovery, and Education". There are two pieces to AI-VERDE, the AI-VERDE chat interface and the AI-VERDE API (application programming interface).

Our chat interface provides you with an interactive, AI-powered assistant designed to enhance your learning, research, and teaching experiences. Using language models from commercial providers and CyVerse's on-premise infrastructure, this interface allows you to engage with an advanced AI assistant capable of answering questions, offering explanations, and assisting with various tasks in real time.

items.title: Key Features
items.text:
• Interactive Q&A: Simply type your question, and the assistant will provide clear, concise answers on a wide range of topics.
  • Designed for small teams and courses: Use AI-VERDE for small teams, labs, and courses.
  • Bring Your Own (BYO) LLM: Instructors and team leads can optionally bring their own commercial or third-party LLM to AI-VERDE or use CyVerse's on-premise LLMs.
  • Built for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Instructors and team leads can optionally configure AI-VERDE to provide answers strictly from source documents.
  • Budget management and cost savings: If you're using commercial services, tokens cost money. Use AI-VERDE to control model access, with budgets for each course or team and per individual (budgets are set by CyVerse on request).
  • Built-in Guardrails: Ensure the responsible, safe, and effective use of AI-VERDE within your team and course.

items.title: Getting Started with AI-VERDE Chat
items.text: This guide will help you get up and running quickly, so you can start making the most out of your experience with our AI-VERDE Chat.

items.title: 1. Sign In
items.text:
Before using the AI-VERDE chat interface, ensure you are signed in with your institution's credentials.

Note

AI-VERDE is currently only available to the University of Arizona community.

  1. Go to https://chat.cyverse.ai/.
  2. Click the Sign In button. You will be taken to CILogon.
  3. On CILogon, select your identity provider. For University of Arizona users, select The University of Arizona.
  4. Click the Log On button.
  5. Log in with your institution’s login process (for University of Arizona users, your NetID).
  6. You will be returned to AI-VERDE, signed in.

items.title: 2. Select Your Team or Course
items.text: Once signed in, find your course or team card and click on the chat button.

items.title: 3. Ask Your First Question
items.text:
After clicking on the course or team card, the page will show a text box where you can interact with AI-VERDE. You can then:

  • Type a question directly in the chat box (e.g., "Why is the sky blue?").
  • Press Send to submit.
  • Receive a Response within seconds, tailored to your query.

items.title: 4. Continue the Conversation
items.text: You can ask follow-up questions for further clarification, request examples, or explore related topics.

items.title: Example
items.text:
1. Initial Question: "Explain the concept of ecosystems in biology."
  2. Follow-Up: "Can you provide examples of different types of ecosystems?"
  3. Further Detail: "How does biodiversity impact ecosystem stability?"

items.title: Tips for Using the Chat Interface
items.text:
• Be Specific: Detailed questions yield the best responses.
  • Explore Broadly: If your team or course is not targeting specific documents, you can ask about a wide range of topics or request explanations for academic concepts.
  • Engage in Multi-Step Conversations: If you need deeper insights, use follow-up questions to refine the responses.

items.title: Usage Budgets
items.text: Each course or team has a usage budget, and some courses also set a budget for each student. By default, budgets are monthly and reset on the 1st of each month. Some courses use a different reset schedule. If you reach your budget, you can use AI-VERDE again once it resets. Ask your instructor or team lead if you're unsure which schedule applies.

items.title: Introduction to AI-VERDE API
items.text: AI-VERDE exposes an OpenAI-compatible API, so any tool or library that supports OpenAI can connect to it using your AI-VERDE API key. AI-VERDE also accepts Anthropic-style requests (used by Claude Code and the Anthropic SDK) and, for Claude Code only, AWS Bedrock-style requests for Claude models hosted on AWS Bedrock. This section explains how to get your key and use it across a range of environments.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text:
Before using the API you will need to:

  1. Obtain your API key — Sign in at chat.cyverse.ai, open your course or team details, and copy the key from the API Key tab. See Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key for step-by-step instructions.
  2. Know which models are available — Your available models are listed on the same API Key page. You can also retrieve them programmatically; see Getting a List of Models.

items.title: What's in This Section
items.text: Section What it covers Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models Claude models on AWS Bedrock with Claude Code and the Claude Code for VS Code extension Using Your API Key in Code Python integration with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and the Anthropic Python SDK Using CLI Coding Assistants Terminal-based AI coding tools: Claude Code Router, Aider, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode Using IDEs VS Code integration: Claude Code for VS Code and Codex for VS Code Using Desktop Clients GUI chat clients such as Chatbox AI

items.title: Base URL and Authentication
items.text:
When configuring a client, you need your API key (copied from the AI-VERDE dashboard) and a base URL. The base URL depends on which style of API the client speaks:

API style Base URL Used by OpenAI-compatible https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 Aider, Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code Router, Chatbox AI, Codex for VS Code, and most OpenAI clients Anthropic-style https://llm-api.cyverse.ai Claude Code (Anthropic models), Claude Code (non-Anthropic models), Claude Code for VS Code, Anthropic Python SDK AWS Bedrock https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock Claude Code on Bedrock, Claude Code for VS Code on Bedrock

If your course details show a different base URL ending in /v1, use it for OpenAI-compatible clients, remove /v1 for Anthropic-style clients, and replace /v1 with /bedrock for AWS Bedrock.

Note

The LangChain and LlamaIndex examples use LiteLLM's litellm_proxy provider, which takes the base URL without /v1 (https://llm-api.cyverse.ai).

OpenAI-compatible clients send the API key as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>), and Anthropic-style clients may send it in an x-api-key header instead; AI-VERDE accepts either. Each guide shows which setting or environment variable holds the key for that tool.

items.title: Aider
items.text: You can follow these instructions to use your AI-VERDE API Key with Aider, self-described "AI pair programming in your terminal". More information on installing and using Aider can be found here, https://aider.chat.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API Key. See Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key.
  2. Note the model(s) you want to configure for Aider. See Getting a List of Models.
  3. Install Aider. Instructions can be found here, https://aider.chat/#getting-started.
  4. The remaining instructions assume a terminal on macOS or Linux with bash and Aider installed.

items.title: 1. Configuring Aider
items.text:
1. Create a $HOME/.aider.conf.yml file with the following contents:

    openai-api-key: insert-your-aiverde-api-key
openai-api-base: https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1
model: openai/insert-default-model

  2. Replace insert-your-aiverde-api-key with your AI-VERDE API Key.

  3. Replace the text insert-default-model with the AI-VERDE model. For example, to use gemma-4-26b-it, the model field would be set to openai/gemma-4-26b-it. If the model name contains a slash (e.g. my-team/claude-sonnet-5), keep it as is and add openai/ in front (e.g. openai/my-team/claude-sonnet-5).

Warning

$HOME/.aider.conf.yml holds your API key. Keep it in your home directory and don't commit or share it.

Note

This is the minimal configuration needed to use Aider. If you want to set other configuration for any models, you can add a $HOME/.aider.model.metadata.json file. Instructions on the configuration values that can be set in this file can be found here, https://aider.chat/docs/config/adv-model-settings.html.

items.title: 2. Running Aider
items.text:
Run Aider with the following command:

aider

Note

You may get additional prompts if you're not in a git repo and if you have not configured your model further (see note above). You can also run aider with aider --no-show-model-warnings if you prefer to ignore model warnings.

If you are successful entering Aider, congratulations!

items.title: Using Anthropic Python SDK with AI-VERDE
items.text:
Anthropic Python SDK is Anthropic's official Python SDK for interacting with Claude models. AI-VERDE can serve as the backend for the Anthropic Python SDK, routing requests through AI-VERDE's budget controls and guardrails to the Claude models available to your course or team.

Note

The Anthropic Python SDK uses AI-VERDE's Anthropic-style API at https://llm-api.cyverse.ai. It does not use the /bedrock endpoint, which is reserved for Claude Code, even when your Claude models are hosted on AWS Bedrock.
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key and note the AI-VERDE base URL. The base URL used in the script must have the /v1 suffix removed, if present. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the Claude model ID you want to use. Instructions for listing available models can be found here. Model names in AI-VERDE are prefixed with an identifier for your course or team, separated by a dash or a slash (e.g. my-team-claude-sonnet-5 or my-team/claude-sonnet-5).
  3. Install the Anthropic Python SDK with pip install anthropic. More information can be found at https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python.
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: Example Python script using Anthropic Python SDK with AI-VERDE
items.text:
Export the following environment variable for your script.

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"

For example:

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-xyz"

Example script:

import os
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(
    base_url="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai", # Replace with the AI-VERDE base URL if different
    api_key=os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"),
)

message = client.messages.create(
    max_tokens=128,
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Hello, Claude",
        }
    ],
    model="<model name>", # Replace with a Claude model name from your model list
)

print(message.content[0].text)

Note

To obtain the AI-VERDE Anthropic Base URL, strip the /v1 suffix if present.
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: Claude Code (using non-Anthropic Models)
items.text:
You can follow these instructions to use your AI-VERDE API key after installing Claude Code. More information on using Claude Code can be found here, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview.

Note

These instructions assume your course or team is connected to non-Anthropic models. Claude Code still sends Anthropic-style requests; AI-VERDE translates them for the non-Anthropic model.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Your AI-VERDE course or team must have access to at least one non-Anthropic model. Coding agents work best with models that support tool use; see the "Supports Tools" column in Current CyVerse Models.
  2. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key. Instructions can be found here.
  3. Note the model name(s) you want to use. Instructions for listing available models can be found here.
  4. Install Claude Code. Instructions can be found here, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.
  5. The remaining instructions assume a terminal on macOS or Linux with bash and Claude Code installed. On Windows, Option 1 below works the same way, with the file at %USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json.

items.title: 1. Configure Claude Code
items.text: You can use the same model for all tiers (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) or you can use different models for each tier. Use the exact model names as returned by your model list.

items.title: Option 1: ~/.claude/settings.json (recommended)
items.text:
Add the following env section to ~/.claude/settings.json (create the file if it does not exist). Settings in this file apply every time you run Claude Code, in any terminal.

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "<your-ai-verde-api-key>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "<model name for opus-tier model>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "<model name for sonnet-tier model>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "<model name for haiku-tier model>",
    "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "<model name for primary model>"
  }
}

For example:

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "gemma-4-26b-it",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "gemma-4-26b-it",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "gemma-4-26b-it",
    "ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "gemma-4-26b-it"
  }
}

If the file already has other settings, add the env section alongside them rather than replacing the file.

Warning

~/.claude/settings.json holds your API key. Keep the key in this user-level file, not in a project's .claude/settings.json, and don't commit or share it.

items.title: Option 2: Shell environment variables
items.text:
Alternatively, export the same variables in your terminal before launching Claude Code:

export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="<model name for opus-tier model>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="<model name for sonnet-tier model>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="<model name for haiku-tier model>"
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="<model name for primary model>"

Exported variables only last for the current terminal session. To avoid re-entering them each session, add the lines to your shell profile (e.g. ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc), then source your shell profile.

Note

To obtain the AI-VERDE Anthropic Base URL, simply remove /v1 (e.g. https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 => https://llm-api.cyverse.ai). If both ~/.claude/settings.json and your shell set the same variable, the value in ~/.claude/settings.json is used.

items.title: 2. Start Claude Code
items.text:
You can then run Claude Code.

claude

The first time Claude Code detects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, it asks whether to use the custom API key. Select Yes. You can run /status inside Claude Code to confirm the base URL and API key it is using.

items.title: If you need to change your ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
items.text: If for some reason you need to change your AI-VERDE API key, update ANTHROPIC_API_KEY wherever you set it in step 1 (~/.claude/settings.json or your shell profile), then restart Claude Code. If you previously declined the key prompt, Claude Code ignores the key without asking again; re-enable it with the Use custom API key option under /config.

items.title: Claude Code (using Anthropic Models)
items.text:
You can follow these instructions to use your AI-VERDE API key after installing Claude Code. More information on using Claude Code can be found here, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview.

Note

These instructions assume your course or team is connected to Anthropic models (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku from Anthropic, Azure or other providers with Anthropic-style APIs). If you need access to Claude Code using a non-Anthropic model, then see the instructions here or use Claude Code Router.

Note

If your Claude models are hosted on AWS Bedrock, we recommend the Bedrock-style setup instead. The Bedrock setup uses ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN instead of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, because Claude Code only sends ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN when talking to a Bedrock endpoint.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Your AI-VERDE course or team must be configured to use Anthropic models (see instructor or team lead).
  2. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key. Instructions can be found here.
  3. Note the model names for the Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models available to your course or team. Instructions for listing available models can be found here.
  4. Install Claude Code. Instructions can be found here, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.
  5. The remaining instructions assume a terminal on macOS or Linux with bash and Claude Code installed. On Windows, Option 1 below works the same way, with the file at %USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json.

items.title: 1. Configure Claude Code
items.text: Model names in AI-VERDE are prefixed with an identifier for your course or team, separated by a dash or a slash (e.g. my-team-claude-sonnet-5 or my-team/claude-sonnet-5). Use the exact names from your model list; Anthropic's public model IDs (e.g. claude-sonnet-5) will not work.

items.title: Option 1: ~/.claude/settings.json (recommended)
items.text:
Add the following env section to ~/.claude/settings.json (create the file if it does not exist). Settings in this file apply every time you run Claude Code, in any terminal.

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "<your-ai-verde-api-key>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "<model name for opus>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "<model name for sonnet>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "<model name for haiku>"
  }
}

For example:

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "my-team-claude-opus-5",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "my-team-claude-sonnet-5",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "my-team-claude-haiku-4-5"
  }
}

If the file already has other settings, add the env section alongside them rather than replacing the file.

Warning

~/.claude/settings.json holds your API key. Keep the key in this user-level file, not in a project's .claude/settings.json, and don't commit or share it.

items.title: Option 2: Shell environment variables
items.text:
Alternatively, export the same variables in your terminal before launching Claude Code:

export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="<model name for opus>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="<model name for sonnet>"

Exported variables only last for the current terminal session. To avoid re-entering them each session, add the lines to your shell profile (e.g. ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc), then source your shell profile.

Note

To obtain the AI-VERDE Anthropic Base URL, simply remove /v1 (e.g. https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 => https://llm-api.cyverse.ai). If both ~/.claude/settings.json and your shell set the same variable, the value in ~/.claude/settings.json is used.

items.title: 2. Start Claude Code
items.text:
You can then run Claude Code.

claude

The first time Claude Code detects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, it asks whether to use the custom API key. Select Yes. You can run /status inside Claude Code to confirm the base URL and API key it is using.

To use Claude Code inside VS Code, see Claude Code for VS Code.

items.title: If you need to change your ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
items.text: If for some reason you need to change your AI-VERDE API key, update ANTHROPIC_API_KEY wherever you set it in step 1 (~/.claude/settings.json or your shell profile), then restart Claude Code. If you previously declined the key prompt, Claude Code ignores the key without asking again; re-enable it with the Use custom API key option under /config.

items.title: Codex
items.text: You can follow these instructions to use your AI-VERDE API key after installing Codex. More information on using Codex can be found here, https://github.com/openai/codex.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the model name you want to use. Instructions for listing available models can be found here. Coding agents work best with models that support tool use; see the "Supports Tools" column in Current CyVerse Models.
  3. Install Codex. Instructions can be found here, https://github.com/openai/codex.
  4. The remaining instructions assume a terminal on macOS or Linux with bash and Codex installed. Windows notes are included where the steps differ.

items.title: 1. Set up the Codex configuration file
items.text:
Codex saves its configuration at ~/.codex/config.toml (%USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml on Windows). Add the following content to the configuration file (replace lines in existing content where appropriate), replacing <your-model-name> with the model you'd like to use.

model = "<your-model-name>"
model_provider = "ai-verde"
model_reasoning_effort = "medium" # change this if you want to adjust the reasoning effort for the model
approvals_reviewer = "user" # change this if you want to adjust the reviewer for approvals, the other option is "auto_review"

[model_providers.ai-verde]
name = "ai-verde"
base_url = "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1"
env_key = "VERDE_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
stream_idle_timeout_ms = 600000 # 10 minutes
stream_max_retries = 5
request_max_retries = 4

For example, your existing ~/.codex/config.toml file may look like this:

model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "high"
approvals_reviewer = "auto_review"

[projects."/home/my_user/my_git_repo_1"]
trust_level = "trusted"

After the update, your ~/.codex/config.toml file should look like this:

model = "gemma-4-26b-it"
model_provider = "ai-verde"
model_reasoning_effort = "medium"
approvals_reviewer = "user"

[model_providers.ai-verde]
name = "ai-verde"
base_url = "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1"
env_key = "VERDE_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
stream_idle_timeout_ms = 600000 # 10 minutes
stream_max_retries = 5
request_max_retries = 4

[projects."/home/my_user/my_git_repo_1"]
trust_level = "trusted"

Export the following environment variable before launching Codex (replacing <your-ai-verde-api-key> with your AI-VERDE API key).

export VERDE_API_KEY="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"

To avoid re-entering this each session, add the line to your shell profile (e.g. ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc). Then, you can source your shell profile.

Tip

On Windows, set the variable permanently in PowerShell with setx VERDE_API_KEY "<your-ai-verde-api-key>", then open a new terminal before launching Codex.

Alternatively, you can save the key in ~/.codex/.env (%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.env on Windows), which Codex loads on startup, instead of exporting it:

VERDE_API_KEY=sk-xxx

This file holds your API key, so don't commit or share it.

items.title: 2. Start Codex
items.text:
You can then run Codex.

codex

items.title: If you need to change your VERDE_API_KEY
items.text: If for some reason you need to change your AI-VERDE API key, update VERDE_API_KEY wherever you set it (your shell profile or ~/.codex/.env), then restart Codex.

items.title: Using your AI-VERDE API key to integrate with LangChain
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the model name you want to use. Instructions for listing available models can be found here.
  3. Install Python 3 with pip.
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: 1. Install LangChain Python libraries
items.text: pip install langchain-litellm
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: 2. Write a Python script
items.text:
Replace [MODEL NAME] with a model name from your model list, keeping the litellm_proxy/ prefix (e.g. litellm_proxy/gemma-4-26b-it). LiteLLM's litellm_proxy provider takes the base URL without /v1.

from langchain_litellm import ChatLiteLLM

llm = ChatLiteLLM(
    model="litellm_proxy/[MODEL NAME]",
    api_key="[AI-VERDE API KEY]",
    api_base="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
)

print(llm.invoke("Hello, world!"))

Alternatively, you can include the API key as an environment variable or secret to avoid storing it in plain text:

import getpass
import os

if not os.environ.get("VERDE_API_KEY"):
    os.environ["VERDE_API_KEY"] = getpass.getpass("Enter AI-VERDE API key: ")
api_key = os.environ["VERDE_API_KEY"]

from langchain_litellm import ChatLiteLLM

llm = ChatLiteLLM(
    model="litellm_proxy/[MODEL NAME]",
    api_key=api_key,
    api_base="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
)

print(llm.invoke("Hello, world!"))
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: Using your AI-VERDE API key to integrate with LlamaIndex
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the model name you want to use. Instructions for listing available models can be found here.
  3. Install Python 3 with pip.
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: 1. Install LlamaIndex libraries
items.text: pip install llama-index-core llama-index-llms-litellm
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: 2. Write a Python script
items.text:
Replace [MODEL NAME] with a model name from your model list, keeping the litellm_proxy/ prefix (e.g. litellm_proxy/gemma-4-26b-it). LiteLLM's litellm_proxy provider takes the base URL without /v1.

from llama_index.llms.litellm import LiteLLM
from llama_index.core.llms import ChatMessage

llm = LiteLLM(
    model="litellm_proxy/[MODEL NAME]",
    api_base="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    api_key="[AI-VERDE API KEY]",
)

message = ChatMessage(role="user", content="Hey! how's it going?")
response = llm.chat([message])

print(response)

Alternatively, you can include the API key as an environment variable or secret to avoid storing it in plain text:

import getpass
import os

if not os.environ.get("VERDE_API_KEY"):
    os.environ["VERDE_API_KEY"] = getpass.getpass("Enter AI-VERDE API key: ")
api_key = os.environ["VERDE_API_KEY"]

from llama_index.llms.litellm import LiteLLM
from llama_index.core.llms import ChatMessage

llm = LiteLLM(
    model="litellm_proxy/[MODEL NAME]",
    api_base="https://llm-api.cyverse.ai",
    api_key=api_key,
)

message = ChatMessage(role="user", content="Hey! how's it going?")
response = llm.chat([message])

print(response)

Note

LlamaIndex embedding support is outlined here, but functionality depends on access to an embedding model through AI-VERDE.
path: Using Your API Key in Code

items.title: Getting a List of Models
items.text:
There are three ways to obtain a list of models:

  1. Go to this page to view the list of CyVerse models. This list does not include models from external inference services e.g., Jetstream2.
  2. Viewing your models in the Course Details.
  3. Using your API Key to view your models.

Models hosted by CyVerse (listed on Current CyVerse Models) have no prefix, e.g. gemma-4-26b-it. Models provided for your course or team are prefixed with an identifier for your course or team, separated by a dash or a slash (e.g. my-team-claude-sonnet-5 or my-team/claude-sonnet-5). Always use the exact name from your model list.

items.title: Viewing your models in the Course Details
items.text:
Your available models will be visible in the AI-VERDE application. These are the steps:

  1. Go to https://chat.cyverse.ai.
  2. After successfully logging in, click the Details button of your course.
  3. Click the "API Key" tab.
  4. The "Available Models" section lists all the models your course has access to.

items.title: Using your API Key to view your models
items.text:
After obtaining your API key from your course/team, store it in an environment variable:

export VERDE_API_KEY="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"

Then list your available models using curl:

curl -s -L "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERDE_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json'

Alternatively, you can use jq or python's json module to view the output in a more human readable format.

Option 1: If you have jq installed:

curl -s -L "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERDE_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json'|jq

Option 2: If you have Python installed (json.tool is part of the standard library):

curl -s -L "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERDE_API_KEY" |python -m json.tool

items.title: OpenCode
items.text: OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent for the terminal. It can read and edit code in your project and run commands, using any model you configure.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the model name(s) you want to use. Instructions for listing available models can be found here. Coding agents work best with models that support tool use; see the "Supports Tools" column in Current CyVerse Models.
  3. Install OpenCode. Instructions can be found here, https://opencode.ai/.
  4. The remaining instructions assume a terminal on macOS or Linux with bash and OpenCode installed.

items.title: 1. Set up the OpenCode configuration file
items.text:
OpenCode uses a configuration file to define custom providers and models. The configuration file is located at either of the following locations:

  • (Mac/Linux) ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
  • (Mac/Linux) ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc (jsonc is a superset of json that allows comments)

Here is an example configuration file for OpenCode that uses the AI-VERDE provider and models:

{
  "provider": {
    "ai-verde": { // this is the identifier for the provider, you can choose any name you like, it needs to be unique in the provider list
      "name": "AI-VERDE", // this is the display name of the provider (what is shown by the `/models` command), you can choose any name you like
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", // this is the npm package that provides the provider's API, use `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` unless you know what you are doing
      "models": {
        "gemma-4-26b-it": { // this is the model name shown in AI-VERDE
            "name": "my-gemma-4-26b-it" // this is the display name of the model (what is shown by the `/models` command), you can choose any name you like
        }
      },
      "options": {
        "apiKey": "{env:VERDE_API_KEY}", // reads your AI-VERDE API key from the VERDE_API_KEY environment variable
        "baseURL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1", // this is the base URL for AI-VERDE, copy-paste from the same page where you got your API Key
        "timeout": 600000 // optional, this is the timeout in milliseconds for API requests, default is 600000 (10 minutes)
      }
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json"
}

Then export your API key before launching OpenCode (replacing <your-ai-verde-api-key> with your AI-VERDE API key):

export VERDE_API_KEY="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"

To avoid re-entering this each session, add the line to your shell profile (e.g. ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc), then source your shell profile.

items.title: 2. Start OpenCode
items.text:
You can then run OpenCode.

opencode

Run /models and select the model you want to use. Run /models again to switch models during a session.

items.title: If you need to change your API Key
items.text: If for some reason you need to change your AI-VERDE API key, re-set the VERDE_API_KEY environment variable (and your shell profile, if you added it there), then restart OpenCode.

items.title: Using Claude Code for VS Code with AI-VERDE
items.text:
Claude Code for VS Code is Anthropic's official extension for using Claude Code within VS Code. AI-VERDE can serve as the backend for the extension through AI-VERDE's Anthropic-style API, routing requests through AI-VERDE's budget controls and guardrails.

Tip

If your course or team's Claude models are hosted on AWS Bedrock, we recommend the Bedrock-style setup instead. Ask your instructor or team lead if you're unsure where your models are hosted.
path: Claude Code for VS Code (using Anthropic Models)

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Your AI-VERDE course or team must be configured to use Anthropic models (see instructor or team lead).
  2. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key. Instructions can be found here.
  3. Note the model names for the Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models available to your course or team. Instructions for listing available models can be found here. Model names in AI-VERDE are prefixed with an identifier for your course or team, separated by a dash or a slash (e.g. my-team-claude-sonnet-5 or my-team/claude-sonnet-5). Anthropic's public model IDs (e.g. claude-sonnet-5) will not work.
  4. Install VS Code. Instructions can be found at https://code.visualstudio.com/download.

items.title: Configuring Environment Variables
items.text:
Next you will need to configure the extension to use AI-VERDE as the backend. Set these in the extension's own "Claude Code: Environment Variables" setting. The extension checks this setting before launching, so it is the reliable place for your AI-VERDE credentials; values in ~/.claude/settings.json do not reach the extension's login check.

Find the setting entry "Claude Code: Environment Variables" and click on "Edit in settings.json".

You will need to add the following environment variables to the claudeCode.environmentVariables section of the settings:

  • add the AI-VERDE Anthropic base URL as ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
  • add your AI-VERDE API key as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
  • add your team model names for Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku
    "claudeCode.environmentVariables": [
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL", "value": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "value": "<your-ai-verde-api-key>"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL", "value": "<model name for opus>"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL", "value": "<model name for sonnet>"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL", "value": "<model name for haiku>"}
    ],

For example, with the values filled in:

    "claudeCode.environmentVariables": [
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL", "value": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "value": "sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL", "value": "my-team-claude-opus-5"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL", "value": "my-team-claude-sonnet-5"},
        { "name": "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL", "value": "my-team-claude-haiku-4-5"}
    ],

Warning

This setting holds your API key. Add it to your VS Code user settings, not to a project's .vscode/settings.json, so the key doesn't get committed with your code.

Note

To obtain the AI-VERDE Anthropic base URL, simply remove /v1 (e.g. https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 => https://llm-api.cyverse.ai).

Note

This setting only applies to the VS Code extension. To use Claude Code in the terminal as well, configure it separately as described in Claude Code (using Anthropic Models).

items.title: Using Codex for VS Code with AI-VERDE
items.text: Codex is OpenAI's official extension for using Codex within VS Code. The extension reads the same configuration as the Codex CLI, so once Codex is set up to use AI-VERDE on your machine, the extension uses AI-VERDE too.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the model name you want to use. Instructions for listing available models can be found here. Coding agents work best with models that support tool use; see the "Supports Tools" column in Current CyVerse Models.
  3. Install VS Code. Instructions can be found at https://code.visualstudio.com/download.

items.title: 1. Configure Codex to use AI-VERDE
items.text: Follow step 1 of the Codex guide to add the ai-verde provider and your model to ~/.codex/config.toml (%USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml on Windows). The extension reads this file. You don't need to install the Codex CLI itself for the extension to work.

items.title: Save your API key in ~/.codex/.env
items.text:
The extension has no setting for environment variables, and it doesn't load your shell profile when VS Code starts from a desktop launcher. A VERDE_API_KEY exported in ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc may never reach it. Save the key in ~/.codex/.env (%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.env on Windows) instead. Codex loads this file on startup.

VERDE_API_KEY=<your-ai-verde-api-key>

For example, with the value filled in:

VERDE_API_KEY=sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

Warning

This file holds your API key. Don't commit or share it.

Note

The Codex CLI reads the same ~/.codex/.env file, so this also sets up codex in the terminal.

items.title: 2. Install the "Codex" extension from OpenAI
items.text: Within the extension marketplace, search for "Codex" and install "Codex – OpenAI's coding agent" published by OpenAI.

items.title: 3. Restart VS Code
items.text: Restart VS Code so the extension picks up your configuration and API key. If you change ~/.codex/config.toml or ~/.codex/.env later, restart VS Code again.

Open the Codex sidebar by clicking the Codex icon in the editor title bar:

items.title: Using AI-VERDE with AWS Bedrock
items.text:
AWS Bedrock is Amazon's fully managed service for accessing foundation models from leading AI providers. AI-VERDE allows users to use AWS Bedrock-provided Anthropic Claude models with Claude Code, both in the terminal and in the VS Code extension.

Note

Currently, the subsequent instructions focus on using Anthropic Claude models from AWS Bedrock. As other models are provided, the instructions will be updated.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
Before connecting Claude Code to AI-VERDE, you will need:

  • An AI-VERDE API key — sign in at chat.cyverse.ai, open your course or team details, and copy the key from the API Key tab. See Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key for step-by-step instructions.
  • The AI-VERDE Bedrock base URL: https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock (or the URL shown in your course details, with /v1 replaced by /bedrock).
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
AI-VERDE acts as a proxy between your application and the underlying model. When you send a request to the AI-VERDE endpoint, AI-VERDE authenticates it against your team or course budget, applies any configured guardrails, then forwards the request to the appropriate model — which may be hosted on AWS Bedrock. For Claude Code, AI-VERDE exposes a Bedrock-compatible endpoint at /bedrock, so Claude Code can use its built-in Bedrock support while AI-VERDE handles authentication and budgets. Other clients should use AI-VERDE's OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-style endpoints instead; see Base URL and Authentication.

Note

The Bedrock-style endpoint is only intended for Claude Code. To call Claude models from your own code, use the Anthropic Python SDK, which uses the Anthropic-style API.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Using Claude Code with AI-VERDE
items.text:
Claude Code is Anthropic's official CLI coding assistant. AI-VERDE can serve as the backend for Claude Code, routing requests through AI-VERDE's budget controls and guardrails to Anthropic Claude models hosted on AWS Bedrock.

Tip

If your course or team's Claude models are hosted on AWS Bedrock, we recommend using this Bedrock-style setup with Claude Code rather than the Anthropic-style setup. Ask your instructor or team lead if you're unsure where your models are hosted.

Note

Unlike the non-Bedrock Claude Code setup, which uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, the Bedrock setup must put your AI-VERDE API key in ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN. When talking to a Bedrock endpoint, Claude Code only sends ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN; an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY would be ignored.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API key and note the AI-VERDE base URL. The base URL used in the environment variables ends in /bedrock rather than /v1. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the Claude model ID for Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. Instructions for listing available models can be found here. Model names in AI-VERDE are prefixed with an identifier for your course or team, separated by a dash or a slash (e.g. my-team-claude-sonnet-5 or my-team/claude-sonnet-5).
  3. Install Claude Code. Instructions can be found at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.
  4. The remaining instructions assume a terminal on macOS or Linux with bash and Claude Code installed. On Windows, Option 1 below works the same way, with the file at %USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: 1. Configure Claude Code
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Option 1: ~/.claude/settings.json (recommended)
items.text:
Add the following env section to ~/.claude/settings.json (create the file if it does not exist). Settings in this file apply every time you run Claude Code, in any terminal.

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "<your-ai-verde-api-key>",
    "ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH": "1",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK": "1",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "<model name for opus>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "<model name for sonnet>",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "<model name for haiku>"
  }
}

For example:

{
  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "sk-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL": "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH": "1",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK": "1",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL": "my-team-claude-opus-5",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL": "my-team-claude-sonnet-5",
    "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL": "my-team-claude-haiku-4-5"
  }
}

If the file already has other settings, add the env section alongside them rather than replacing the file.

Warning

~/.claude/settings.json holds your API key. Keep the key in this user-level file, not in a project's .claude/settings.json, and don't commit or share it.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Option 2: Shell environment variables
items.text:
Alternatively, export the same variables in your terminal before launching Claude Code:

export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="<your-ai-verde-api-key>"
export ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL=https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock
export CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH=1
export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL="<model name for opus>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="<model name for sonnet>"
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL="<model name for haiku>"

Exported variables only last for the current terminal session. To avoid re-entering them each session, add the lines to your shell profile (e.g. ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc), then source your shell profile.

Note

To obtain the AI-VERDE Bedrock Base URL, simply substitute /v1 with /bedrock, e.g. https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 to https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock. If both ~/.claude/settings.json and your shell set the same variable, the value in ~/.claude/settings.json is used.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: 2. Launch Claude Code
items.text:
Start Claude Code:

claude

You can run /status inside Claude Code to confirm it is using Amazon Bedrock with the AI-VERDE base URL.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: If you need to change your API Key
items.text: If for some reason you need to change your AI-VERDE API key, update ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN wherever you set it in step 1 (~/.claude/settings.json or your shell profile), then restart Claude Code.
path: Using Your API Key for AWS Bedrock Models

items.title: Chatbox AI
items.text: Chatbox AI is a chat client that works on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, and the web. These instructions are written for the Windows and macOS desktop versions; other versions vary slightly.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API Key. Instructions can be found here.
  2. Note the model(s) you want to configure for Chatbox AI. Instructions can be found here.
  3. Install Chatbox AI by visiting this page: https://chatboxai.app/en#download.
  4. The remaining instructions assume you have Chatbox AI installed.

items.title: 1. Configure AI-VERDE in Chatbox AI
items.text:
For these steps, you can refer to the screenshots below.

  1. Launch Chatbox AI.
  2. Click Settings.
  3. Click Model Provider.
  4. Click the "+ Add" button.
  5. Enter "ai-verde" in the Name field.
  6. Leave API Mode set to "OpenAI API Compatible".
  7. Click the Add button. You should then be shown the ai-verde configuration panel on the right.
  8. Enter (or paste) your AI-VERDE Key in the API Key field.
  9. Enter https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 in the API Host field, and leave the API Path field empty.
  10. In the model section, click the "New" button, and a new model dialog box will be shown.
  11. Enter the model in the "Model ID" field.

  12. Under capabilities, select the capabilities you know the model supports: vision, reasoning, or tool use.

    Note

    Capabilities for a model can be modified at a later time.

  13. Click on the "Save" button

  14. You can repeat steps 10-13 to add additional models.
  15. Optionally, after adding one or more models, you can click the "Check" button to test the connection to AI-VERDE.

Now you're ready to begin chatting!

items.title: 2. Using Chatbox AI with configured models
items.text:
1. At any time, you can click the "New Chat" button or click a previous conversation in the left panel.
  2. Select the model for this chat session, if necessary.
  3. Enter your request in the chat textbox to begin chatting with the model.

There is a lot of functionality provided by Chatbox AI (as with many other chat interfaces). Feel free to explore!

items.title: Claude Code Router (using non-Anthropic Models)
items.text: You can follow these instructions to use your AI-VERDE API Key after installing Claude Code and Claude Code Router. More information on installing and using Claude Code Router can be found here, https://github.com/musistudio/claude-code-router.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Obtain your AI-VERDE API Key. See Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key.
  2. Note the model(s) you want to configure for Claude Code. See Getting a List of Models.
  3. Install Claude Code. Instructions can be found here, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.
  4. Install Claude Code Router. Instructions can be found here, https://github.com/musistudio/claude-code-router.
  5. The remaining instructions assume a terminal on macOS or Linux with bash, Claude Code, and Claude Code Router installed.

items.title: 1. Configuring Claude Code Router
items.text:
This step is only needed the first time you use Claude Code Router.

In a terminal, enter the command ccr start:

ccr start

Because no configuration exists yet, you will be prompted to enter the minimum configuration to start Claude Code Router. Use the following table for guidance on the values:

Field Value or Instructions Notes Provider Name ai-verde any string works Provider API KEY enter your AI-VERDE API key Provider URL https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/chat/completions MODEL Name <verde model name> replace <verde model name> with the model you'd like to use

Note

Unlike most OpenAI-compatible clients, Claude Code Router needs the full chat completions endpoint (https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/chat/completions), not the base URL ending in /v1.

After entering the MODEL name, you should see text similar to the following:

Loaded JSON config from: /home/<user>/.claude-code-router/config.json
register transformer: Anthropic (endpoint: /v1/messages)
register transformer: gemini (endpoint: /v1beta/models/:modelAndAction)
register transformer: deepseek (no endpoint)
register transformer: tooluse (no endpoint)
register transformer: openrouter (no endpoint)
register transformer: maxtoken (no endpoint)
providerConfig:  ai-verde undefined
ai-verde provider registered
🚀 LLMs API server listening on http://127.0.0.1:3456
Your configuration is now saved to ~/.claude-code-router/config.json. Press ctrl-c to stop this server; ccr code in the next step starts it again in the background.

items.title: 2. Running Claude Code Router
items.text:
Run Claude Code with Claude Code Router using the following command:

ccr code

If you are successful entering Claude Code, congratulations! To use Claude Code with the same settings, you will need to run ccr code every time.

items.title: Updating Claude Code Router configuration
items.text: At some point, you may want to add other models or add or update configuration options. To do so, you can edit the configuration file found in ~/.claude-code-router/config.json. This file holds your API key, so don't commit or share it.

items.title: Common API Errors
items.text:
When the AI-VERDE API rejects a request, it returns an HTTP error status and a short JSON message. This page explains the errors you are most likely to see, what causes them, and whether you can fix them yourself or need to contact support.

Your client may show the raw JSON, a shortened message, or an exception name. Search the error text for the HTTP status (401, 403, 404, 429, and so on) and the type field, then find the matching section below.

items.title: Quick reference
items.text: Status What it usually means Who can fix it 400 The model name is wrong You 401 Your API key is missing, mistyped, or expired You, or support if the key has expired 403 Your course or team doesn't have access to that model Support 404 The base URL or endpoint path is wrong You 429 with budget_exceeded Your course or team has used up its budget Support 429 without budget_exceeded The model is busy or temporarily unavailable Wait and retry 500 or 503 The model provider is down or unreachable Wait and retry, then support

items.title: What an error looks like
items.text:
Most errors come back as JSON with an error object:

{
    "error": {
        "message": "Authentication Error, No api key passed in.",
        "type": "auth_error",
        "param": "None",
        "code": "401"
    }
}

message describes the problem. type names the error category, but some errors leave it empty (null or the string "None"). code repeats the HTTP status. Rely on the HTTP status first and use the message for detail.

items.title: 401 Unauthorized: the API key was rejected
items.text:
AI-VERDE could not match your request to a valid API key. Common causes:

  • The key is missing from the request, or the client reads it from an environment variable that isn't set in the current shell.
  • The key was copied with extra spaces or a missing character.
  • The key belongs to a course or team that has ended, so it has expired.

The message tells you which case you hit:

Message starts with Cause Authentication Error, No api key passed in. The client didn't send a key Authentication Error, Invalid proxy server token passed. The key doesn't match any AI-VERDE key Authentication Error - Expired Key. The key has expired

To fix it, copy the key again from the API Key tab of your course details (see Obtaining your AI-VERDE API Key) and check that your client sends it. OpenAI-compatible clients send it as a bearer token:

Authorization: Bearer <your-ai-verde-api-key>

You can test the key on its own with curl. If this returns your model list, the key works and the problem is in your client configuration:

curl -s "https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERDE_API_KEY"

Retrying with the same key won't help. If a freshly copied key still fails, or the key has expired, email ai-verde-support@cyverse.org.

Note

Claude Code on AWS Bedrock reads the key from ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Setting the wrong variable produces a 401. See Using Claude Code.

items.title: 401 from the model provider
items.text: Sometimes your key is fine and the 401 comes from the provider behind AI-VERDE, such as AWS Bedrock. In that case the message contains litellm.AuthenticationError followed by the provider's own error text. Getting a new API key won't fix this. Email support with the full error message.

items.title: 400 Bad Request: the model name is wrong
items.text:
AI-VERDE doesn't recognize the model you asked for:

{
    "error": {
        "message": "/chat/completions: Invalid model name passed in model=claude-sonnet-5. Call `/v1/models` to view available models for your key.",
        "type": "None",
        "param": "None",
        "code": "400"
    }
}

This usually happens when you use the provider's public model name instead of the AI-VERDE name. Models provided for your course or team carry a course or team prefix, for example my-team-claude-sonnet-5 or my-team/claude-sonnet-5. CyVerse-hosted models such as gemma-4-26b-it have no prefix.

Copy the exact name from your model list. Getting a List of Models shows how to find it in the course details or with the API.

If the message instead contains litellm.NotFoundError with a 404 status, AI-VERDE recognized the name but the provider couldn't find the model. Email support.

items.title: 403 Forbidden: no access to that model
items.text:
The model exists, but your key isn't allowed to use it:

{
    "error": {
        "message": "key not allowed to access model. This key can only access models=['my-team-gemma-4-26b-it']. Tried to access my-team-claude-sonnet-5",
        "type": "key_model_access_denied",
        "param": "model",
        "code": "403"
    }
}

The message lists the models your key can use. Switch to one of those, or ask your instructor or ai-verde-support@cyverse.org to add the model to your course or team. You may also see team_model_access_denied or user_model_access_denied, which mean the same thing at the team or user level.

items.title: 429 Too Many Requests
items.text: A 429 has two very different causes. Read the message before you retry.

items.title: Budget exceeded
items.text:
Your course, team, or key has spent its budget:

{
    "error": {
        "message": "Budget has been exceeded! Team=team-example Current cost: 10.5, Max budget: 10.0",
        "type": "budget_exceeded",
        "param": null,
        "code": "429"
    }
}

Look for type: "budget_exceeded" or Budget has been exceeded in the message. Retrying won't work. Requests resume after the budget resets or after CyVerse staff raise it. Instructors can't change budgets themselves, so email ai-verde-support@cyverse.org and include the course or team name.

items.title: Model busy or temporarily unavailable
items.text:
If the message says No deployments available or No healthy deployment available, AI-VERDE has no capacity for that model right now. Messages containing litellm.RateLimitError mean the provider is throttling requests.

These clear up on their own. If the response includes a Retry-After header or says Try again in <seconds> seconds, wait that long before retrying. Otherwise, wait a little longer between each retry, or switch to another model from your list for now. If the error lasts more than an hour or so, email support.

items.title: 404 Not Found: wrong URL
items.text:
A request to a URL that AI-VERDE doesn't serve returns this instead of the usual error object:

{
    "detail": "Not Found"
}

Almost always the base URL is wrong for the client you're using. Check it against this table:

Client type Base URL OpenAI-compatible (Codex, OpenCode, Aider, Chatbox AI, OpenAI SDK) https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/v1 Anthropic-style (Claude Code, Anthropic SDK) https://llm-api.cyverse.ai LangChain and LlamaIndex with litellm_proxy https://llm-api.cyverse.ai Claude Code on AWS Bedrock https://llm-api.cyverse.ai/bedrock

OpenAI-compatible clients add /chat/completions to the base URL themselves, so don't include it. A base URL that ends in /v1/v1 or is missing /v1 both produce 404. See Base URL and Authentication for details.

A 405 Method Not Allowed means the path exists but the client used the wrong HTTP method, for example GET on /v1/chat/completions instead of POST.

items.title: 500 and 503: provider problems
items.text:
These errors mean AI-VERDE received your request but couldn't reach the model provider.

Status Message contains Meaning 500 litellm.APIConnectionError AI-VERDE couldn't connect to the provider 503 litellm.ServiceUnavailableError The provider is down 503 no_db_connection AI-VERDE's key database is briefly unreachable

There's nothing to change on your side. Wait a few minutes and retry. If the error persists, email ai-verde-support@cyverse.org with the model name, the time, and the full message.

items.title: Errors in Python code
items.text:
Python libraries turn these HTTP errors into exceptions. The exception name tells you which section above applies.

The OpenAI SDK raises exceptions by HTTP status, such as AuthenticationError for 401, PermissionDeniedError for 403, NotFoundError for 404, and RateLimitError for 429. A budget error and a busy-model error both raise RateLimitError, so check the exception message for budget_exceeded before retrying in a loop.

LangChain and LlamaIndex use LiteLLM under the hood, so you may see LiteLLM exception names:

Exception See litellm.AuthenticationError 401 Unauthorized litellm.PermissionDeniedError 403 Forbidden litellm.NotFoundError 400 Bad Request or 404 Not Found litellm.BudgetExceededError Budget exceeded litellm.RateLimitError Model busy or temporarily unavailable litellm.ServiceUnavailableError, litellm.APIConnectionError 500 and 503

items.title: Contacting support
items.text:
If none of the above fixes the problem, email ai-verde-support@cyverse.org with:

  • the full error message, including the HTTP status
  • the model name you requested
  • the tool or library you're using and its base URL
  • roughly when the error happened

Don't include your API key in the email.

items.title: Request a Course or Team
items.text:
To request a course or team in AI-VERDE, email ai-verde-support@cyverse.org. Use this template to describe your request:

Subject: AI-VERDE course or team request: [course or team name]

Course or team name: [name and course code, if applicable]
Owner: [name and institutional email address]
Start date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
End date: [YYYY-MM-DD, or ongoing]
Expected enrollment: [number of students or team members]
Intended use: [assignments, research tasks, or other activities]

If any details are undecided, note that in your email. You can add your roster after the course or team is created, as described below.

items.title: What Happens Next
items.text:
Once you send your request:

  • CyVerse staff will create your course/team in AI-VERDE.
  • After your course/team is created, it will appear in the AI-VERDE dashboard.
  • CyVerse staff will contact you and the owner (if different) after the course/team is created.

items.title: Adding Your Roster
items.text:
Once your course/team is created, you can add your students, TAs, and co-instructors in either of two ways:

  • Add them yourself in the Members tab of your course. See Managing a Course.
  • Email your roster to ai-verde-support@cyverse.org and CyVerse staff will add the members for you.

items.title: Contact and Feedback
items.text: We’d love your feedback. Please send it to: ai-verde-support@cyverse.org

items.title: Managing a Course in AI-VERDE
items.text: Once your course has been created, you’ll find it listed in your AI-VERDE dashboard. From here, owners and instructors can update course details, manage members, monitor usage, and design AI-powered learning activities.

items.title: Course Overview
items.text:
The Overview tab is your course’s home base. Here, you can:

  • Change the course name and description
  • Update the title to match your course.
  • Add a clear description so students know the purpose.
  • Set start and end dates
  • Determines when the course appears on members’ dashboards.
  • Example: If you set a start date for Sept 1, the course will not appear on students’ dashboards before that date. Students can still sign in to AI-VERDE, but they will not see the course.
  • After the end date, the course no longer appears on members’ dashboards.
  • Adjust course activity status
  • Switch a course to Active when ready for students.
  • Change to Inactive if you want to temporarily hide the course from members’ dashboards without deleting it.

A course appears on members’ dashboards only while it is Active and the current date is between its start and end dates.

items.title: Managing Members
items.text:
The Members tab gives you full control over who is enrolled and what they can do.

Features:

  • Add new members
  • Enter the user’s email address.
  • Assign them a role at the time of adding.
  • Remove members
  • Select a user and remove them from the course.
  • Useful if a student drops the class or a TA changes.
  • Edit member roles
  • Roles determine what access each user has (see below).

items.title: Roles
items.text:
Each course has one Owner and may have any number of Co-owners, in addition to members with the Instructor, TA, or Student role.

Action Owner / Co-owner Instructor TA Student Edit course name, description, dates, and status ✓ ✓ Add and remove members ✓ ✓ ✓ Change a member’s role ✓ ✓ View course and individual usage ✓ ✓ ✓ Create, edit, and delete prompts ✓ ✓ ✓ Use the course chat and course prompts ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Get a personal API key ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓

TAs can add members only with the Student or TA role.

Tip: If a student says they can’t see the course, check the Members tab first to make sure they are listed.

items.title: Budget and Usage
items.text:
AI-VERDE resources are tied to a budget, managed in coordination with the CyVerse team.

  • Budgets are set by CyVerse
  • The course budget and any per-student budgets are set by CyVerse staff. To request a change, email ai-verde-support@cyverse.org.
  • What you can do as an owner, instructor, or TA:
  • View individual usage → see how much each student has consumed.
  • View total course usage → monitor whether the class is approaching budget limits.
  • Why it matters:
  • Helps you plan assignments around available resources.
  • Identifies students who may need guidance if their usage is unusually high.

items.title: AI Prompts and Content
items.text:
The Prompts feature lets instructors and TAs design and share structured prompts for AI activities.

How to use it:

  1. Go to the Prompts tab.
  2. Write a prompt (e.g., “Summarize today’s lecture into 5 key points”) and save it.
  3. Every member of the course can see and use the prompt as soon as it is saved.

This feature helps standardize assignments and ensures all students are working from the same AI instructions.

items.title: API Keys and Integrations
items.text:
Instructors can extend AI-VERDE beyond the platform using API keys.

  • Generate API keys
  • Useful for advanced workflows, automation, or integrating AI-VERDE with other systems. See the AI-VERDE API documentation.
  • Why this matters:
  • Keeps AI-VERDE flexible, fitting into your department’s existing tools rather than operating as an isolated system.

items.title: Troubleshooting While Managing
items.text:
• Course doesn’t show up? → Confirm with support that your course was created, that its status is Active, and that today is between its start and end dates.
  • A student can’t see the course? → Verify they are listed under Members. If not, add them. Also check the course status and dates.
  • Budget concerns? → Email ai-verde-support@cyverse.org to review or request an adjustment.
  • Prompt not working as expected? → Double-check the prompt’s wording and edit it in the Prompts tab; changes are visible to members immediately.
